title: Totality from Deir el-Bahari — Four Nights, 30 July to 3 August
intro: A short, deliberate trip for someone who has already done Egypt once. No cruise, no full tour, no filler: the two museums you have not seen, the Luxor sites you want to see again, and the eclipse itself from the terraces at Deir el-Bahari rather than in the crush at Karnak. The sleeper train does double duty as transport and accommodation, north and south, which keeps two of the four nights off the hotel bill entirely — worth having in the week when every bed in Luxor is charging a premium. One hotel night in Cairo at the start, one in Luxor the night before totality, and private licensed Egyptologists in both cities. Every entrance ticket is included, and so is the entry visa.

arrival.title: Arrival in Cairo — Friday 30 July
arrival.description:
Arrival at Cairo International Airport.
Our representative meets you airside and stays with you through the visa on arrival — which we have included — and the passport and customs formalities.
Private air-conditioned transfer to your hotel.
Nothing scheduled. You know Cairo already, so the evening is simply yours to eat and sleep off the flight.
Overnight in Cairo.
arrival.hotel: Cairo — budget guesthouse / hostel-style (or equal), bed & breakfast

days.title: The Grand Egyptian Museum, the Royal Mummies & the Night Train — Saturday 31 July
days.description:
Breakfast and check-out; your bags travel with you today and you will not need a room tonight.
The Grand Egyptian Museum with your private Egyptologist: the hanging obelisk at the entrance, the Ramses II atrium, the grand staircase of royal statuary, and the complete Tutankhamun collection shown together for the first time — over five thousand objects with the death mask among them. It did not exist last time you were here, and it takes a morning.
Lunch nearby.
The National Museum of Egyptian Civilization at Fustat in the afternoon, and the reason for going: the Royal Mummies Hall. Twenty kings and queens in low light and climate control — Ramses II, Hatshepsut, Seti I — the woman whose temple you will be standing on two days from now among them.
A light supper, then transfer to Giza station for the sleeper to Luxor. Your own cabin, berth made up while you are at the window, and you wake in Upper Egypt.
Overnight on board.

days.title: The East Bank — the Amun Precinct & the Southern Sanctuary — Sunday 1 August
days.description:
Arrival in Luxor early morning, met on the platform and taken to your guesthouse to drop bags, shower and eat.
The great precinct of Amun with your Luxor Egyptologist, out early before the heat: the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes, the first pylon, and the Great Hypostyle Hall — one hundred and thirty-four columns, the tallest twenty-one metres, still carrying their painted architraves.
Beyond the standard route, since you have seen the headline once already: the sacred lake, the Middle Kingdom court at the heart of the complex, the fallen obelisk, and the Botanical Chamber of Tuthmosis III with its carved catalogue of Syrian plants.
Out of the sun through the worst of the afternoon.
Late afternoon at the Southern Sanctuary in the middle of town, joined to the Amun precinct by the restored three-kilometre Avenue of Sphinxes, with the Roman and Islamic city built straight over the top of it — best in the last hour of light and after dark.
Off the beaten path, at no extra cost if you want them instead: the museum on the corniche, the Mummification Museum, or the alabaster workshops at Gurna.
An early night. Overnight in Luxor.
days.hotel: Luxor — budget guesthouse / hostel-style (or equal), bed & breakfast

days.title: Totality from the Terraces at Deir el-Bahari — Monday 2 August
days.description:
A pre-dawn crossing to the west bank and check-out; your bags travel with the vehicle, and you are on the bank before the roads start to close.
The royal tombs at first light, when the valley is at its emptiest: three on the standard ticket with your private Egyptologist, cut deep into the rock with their corridors of painted text and star-vaulted ceilings intact. Tutankhamun, Seti I and Nefertari are separately ticketed and can be added on the spot.
The Valley of the Queens after it — Nefertari's tomb is the finest painted surface in Egypt if you choose to add it, and the valley itself is quiet even today.
Then up to Deir el-Bahari and the Temple of Hatshepsut, in good time, and you stay. Three colonnaded terraces built straight into the cliff at the head of the valley, facing east across the flood plain — which is exactly the right way to be facing. Shade and water; your guide stays with you or leaves you to it, as you prefer.
The partial phases run for over an hour before the light goes wrong and the cliff behind you loses its colour. Then totality, on the terraces of the queen whose face you saw in Cairo on Saturday. Luxor lies close to the point of greatest duration on this eclipse, one of the longest of the century.
We wait for the roads to clear rather than fight them, then a late lunch, a shower at a day-use room, and the evening sleeper north. Overnight on board.

departure.title: Departure — Tuesday 3 August
departure.description:
Arrival at Giza in the early morning, met on the platform.
A day-use room to shower, change and eat a proper breakfast before you travel — nobody wants to fly straight off a sleeper.
Time to spend as you like if your flight is late in the day; say the word and we will put a guide and a car at your disposal for the morning, at extra cost.
Private air-conditioned transfer to Cairo International Airport in good time, with final meet & assist through check-in.
Safe journey home.
